title: Andryusha and Colored Balloons
statementMd:
Andryusha goes through a park each day. The squares and paths between them look boring to Andryusha, so he decided to decorate them.

The park consists of $*n*$ squares connected with $(*n* - 1)$ bidirectional paths in such a way that any square is reachable from any other using these paths. Andryusha decided to hang a colored balloon at each of the squares. The baloons' colors are described by positive integers, starting from $1$. In order to make the park varicolored, Andryusha wants to choose the colors in a special way. More precisely, he wants to use such colors that if $*a*$, $*b*$ and $*c*$ are distinct squares that $*a*$ and $*b*$ have a direct path between them, and $*b*$ and $*c*$ have a direct path between them, then balloon colors on these three squares are distinct.

Andryusha wants to use as little different colors as possible. Help him to choose the colors!

## Input

The first line contains single integer $*n*$ ($3 ≤ *n* ≤ 2·10^{5}$) — the number of squares in the park.

Each of the next $(*n* - 1)$ lines contains two integers $*x*$ and $*y*$ ($1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ *n*$) — the indices of two squares directly connected by a path.

It is guaranteed that any square is reachable from any other using the paths.

## Output

In the first line print single integer $*k*$ — the minimum number of colors Andryusha has to use.

In the second line print $*n*$ integers, the $*i*$-th of them should be equal to the balloon color on the $*i*$-th square. Each of these numbers should be within range from $1$ to $*k*$.

## Note

In the first sample the park consists of three squares: $1 → 3 → 2$. Thus, the balloon colors have to be distinct.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2ff653f32bfeefaf0fd3028981bd2d53dc4b30f6.png) Illustration for the first sample.

In the second example there are following triples of consequently connected squares:

- $1 → 3 → 2$
- $1 → 3 → 4$
- $1 → 3 → 5$
- $2 → 3 → 4$
- $2 → 3 → 5$
- $4 → 3 → 5$

We can see that each pair of squares is encountered in some triple, so all colors have to be distinct.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a7848c3533ce6126dcfebb18b1205cbeb946a885.png) Illustration for the second sample.

In the third example there are following triples:

- $1 → 2 → 3$
- $2 → 3 → 4$
- $3 → 4 → 5$

We can see that one or two colors is not enough, but there is an answer that uses three colors only.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/56b03c0b57412feb7b6b81122b439709cce143fd.png) Illustration for the third sample.
statementZhMd:
安德留沙每天都会经过一个公园。公园里的方格和连接它们的小路让安德留沙觉得很无聊，因此他决定装饰这个公园。

这个公园由 $*n*$ 个方格组成，它们之间由 $(*n* - 1)$ 条双向小路连接，并且任意一个方格都可以通过这些小路到达其他任意方格。安德留沙决定在每个方格上悬挂一个彩色气球。气球的颜色用从 $1$ 开始的正整数表示。为了让公园变得五彩缤纷，安德留沙希望以一种特殊的方式选择颜色。更准确地说，他希望使用满足以下条件的颜色：如果 $*a*$、$*b*$ 和 $*c*$ 是三个不同的方格，且 $*a*$ 与 $*b*$ 之间有一条直接相连的小路，$*b*$ 与 $*c*$ 之间也有一条直接相连的小路，那么这三个方格上的气球颜色必须互不相同。

安德留沙希望使用尽可能少的不同颜色。请帮助他选择颜色！

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$3 ≤ *n* ≤ 2·10^{5}$）——公园中方格的数量。

接下来的 $(*n* - 1)$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 $*x*$ 和 $*y*$（$1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ *n*$），表示两个通过小路直接连接的方格的编号。

保证任意一个方格都可以通过这些小路到达其他任意方格。

## 输出格式

第一行输出一个整数 $*k*$——安德留沙需要使用的最少颜色数。

第二行输出 $*n*$ 个整数，其中第 $*i*$ 个整数应等于第 $*i*$ 个方格上的气球颜色。这些数都必须在 $1$ 到 $*k*$ 的范围内。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，公园由三个方格组成：$1 → 3 → 2$。因此，气球的颜色必须互不相同。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2ff653f32bfeefaf0fd3028981bd2d53dc4b30f6.png) 第一个样例的示意图。

在第二个样例中，存在以下由小路依次连接的方格三元组：

- $1 → 3 → 2$
- $1 → 3 → 4$
- $1 → 3 → 5$
- $2 → 3 → 4$
- $2 → 3 → 5$
- $4 → 3 → 5$

可以看到，任意一对方格都会出现在某个三元组中，因此所有颜色都必须互不相同。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a7848c3533ce6126dcfebb18b1205cbeb946a885.png) 第二个样例的示意图。

在第三个样例中，存在以下三元组：

- $1 → 2 → 3$
- $2 → 3 → 4$
- $3 → 4 → 5$

可以看到，使用一种或两种颜色是不够的，但存在一个只使用三种颜色的方案。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/56b03c0b57412feb7b6b81122b439709cce143fd.png) 第三个样例的示意图。
